title: Infrastructure
description: Vulnerabilities in network perimeters, unauthenticated administrative datastores, virtualization daemons, and legacy protocols.

attacks.name: Open ports / unnecessary services
attacks.desc: Exposing non-essential management daemons, legacy test ports, and unhardened network services directly to the public Internet without firewall rules.
attacks.prevention: Remove unnecessary network listeners and restrict required ports with host and network firewalls.

attacks.name: Exposed databases
attacks.desc: Leaving production database engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB) accessible to the public Internet without IP filtering, opening avenues for automated credential brute-forcing.
attacks.prevention: Keep databases on private networks, require authentication and TLS, and restrict inbound access to application hosts.

attacks.name: Unauthenticated Redis
attacks.desc: Deploying Redis instances without password authentication, allowing attackers to read/write in-memory data, overwrite authorized_keys, or write malicious crontabs.
attacks.prevention: Bind Redis to a private interface, require authentication and ACLs, and block public network access.

attacks.name: Open Elasticsearch
attacks.desc: Exposing Elasticsearch HTTP REST APIs (port 9200) without authentication, enabling arbitrary search queries, document deletion, and complete cluster indexing exfiltration.
attacks.prevention: Require Elasticsearch authentication and network restrictions; expose only intended APIs through a secured gateway.

attacks.name: Exposed Docker API
attacks.desc: Leaving Docker engine TCP sockets exposed without mutual TLS, allowing attackers to spin up privileged containers mounting the host filesystem for instant root takeover.
attacks.prevention: Do not expose the Docker API publicly; use protected sockets and narrowly scoped access for automation.

attacks.name: Exposed Kubernetes API
attacks.desc: Allowing anonymous access to Kubernetes API servers (port 6443) or kubelet endpoints (port 10250), permitting pod creation, secret extraction, and cluster compromise.
attacks.prevention: Disable anonymous Kubernetes API access and require RBAC, network controls, and audited credentials.

attacks.name: Exposed CI/CD
attacks.desc: Exposing continuous integration controllers without strict authentication, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary pipeline scripts and steal build secrets.
attacks.prevention: Protect CI/CD interfaces with SSO and MFA, patch them, and restrict access to trusted networks.

attacks.name: Exposed monitoring
attacks.desc: Leaving infrastructure monitoring dashboards open without authentication, revealing network topologies, environment variables, internal hostnames, and application metrics.
attacks.prevention: Require authentication for monitoring dashboards and redact sensitive metrics and labels.

attacks.name: SNMP enumeration
attacks.desc: Querying Simple Network Management Protocol agents using default community strings ('public', 'private') to map hardware specs, routing tables, and interface addresses.

attacks.name: SMB / NetBIOS enumeration
attacks.desc: Establishing anonymous or guest SMB sessions across ports 139/445 to list network shares, active domain users, password policies, and system services.

attacks.name: Anonymous FTP
attacks.desc: Permitting anonymous logins on FTP servers, allowing unauthorized visitors to download proprietary assets or upload malicious webshells into web roots.

attacks.name: Open SMTP relay
attacks.desc: Misconfiguring mail transfer agents to accept and deliver unauthenticated email destined for external domains, turning servers into spam and phishing relays.

attacks.name: DNS misconfig
attacks.desc: Omitting or misconfiguring SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policy records, allowing cybercriminals to forge and deliver spoofed emails appearing to originate from the legitimate corporate domain.

attacks.name: Email spoofing
attacks.desc: Exploiting missing domain email authentication policies to send forged email communications to customers and employees for credential harvesting and invoice fraud.

attacks.name: IPv6 exposure
attacks.desc: Enabling dual-stack IPv6 routing where hosts lack the rigorous firewall rules and intrusion detection protections applied to primary IPv4 interfaces.

attacks.name: Cloud metadata service abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting SSRF or uncontained local code execution to query Instance Metadata Service v1 (which lacks header tokens) to steal instance IAM role keys.

attacks.name: Pivoting into internal network
attacks.desc: Using a compromised perimeter web server as a network proxy (via SSH tunnels, chisel, or socat) to route traffic into protected corporate and VPC subnets.

attacks.name: Outdated software / CVE matching
attacks.desc: Running unpatched operating system packages, web servers (Apache, Nginx), or runtimes containing published high-severity CVEs with known public exploit scripts.

attacks.name: Public PoC application
attacks.desc: Applying publicly available Proof of Concept exploit code against vulnerable internet-facing applications and perimeter infrastructure.

attacks.name: Banner grabbing
attacks.desc: Connecting to open TCP/UDP sockets to inspect returned service banners, software names, and operating system build information for targeted vulnerability mapping.

attacks.name: Network topology mapping
attacks.desc: Analyzing network hops, ICMP responses, and TCP packet TTL behaviors to determine perimeter firewall layouts, NAT gateways, and load balancer configurations.

attacks.name: VPN / portal exposure
attacks.desc: Targeting internet-facing SSL-VPN gateways (Pulse Secure, Fortinet, Cisco) with known authentication bypasses or unpatched buffer overflow CVEs.

attacks.name: LDAP anonymous bind
attacks.desc: Connecting to LDAP directory servers without credentials to enumerate all domain users, group memberships, computer accounts, and access control lists.

attacks.name: NFS share enumeration
attacks.desc: Mounting Network File System shares exported with 'no_root_squash' or unrestricted IP access to read corporate backups or inject root-owned binaries.
